chunks.text:
Simvastatin belongs to a group of drugs called HMG CoA reductase inhibitors, or "statins."
Simvastatin is used to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (low-density lipoprotein, or LDL).
It is used to increase levels of "good" cholesterol (high-density lipoprotein, or HDL).
It is used to lower triglycerides (a type of fat in the blood).
Simvastatin is used to lower the risk of stroke, heart attack, and other heart complications.
This is done in people with diabetes, coronary heart disease, or other risk factors.
Simvastatin is used in adults and children who are at least 10 years old.

In rare cases, simvastatin can cause a condition.
The condition results in the breakdown of skeletal muscle tissue.
The condition potentially leads to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain.
Call your doctor right away if you have tenderness.
Call your doctor right away if you have weakness.
Call your doctor right away if you have a fever.
Call your doctor right away if you have unusual tiredness.
Call your doctor right away if you have dark colored urine.
Never take simvastatin in larger amounts, or for longer than recommended by your doctor.
Follow your doctor's dosing instructions very carefully.
Taking too much of this medication may cause serious or life-threatening side effects.
Before taking this medicine, tell your doctor if you have ever had liver or kidney disease.
Tell your doctor if you have diabetes.
Tell your doctor if you have a thyroid disorder.
Tell your doctor if you have a muscle weakness condition.
A muscle weakness condition includes myasthenia gravis or ocular myasthenia.
Tell your doctor if you are of Chinese descent.

Take simvastatin exactly as prescribed.
Follow all directions on your prescription label.
Never take simvastatin in larger amounts, or for longer than prescribed.
Taking too much of simvastatin may cause serious or life-threatening side effects.
Simvastatin is usually taken once a day in the evening.
If you are taking the oral suspension, take oral suspension on an empty stomach.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose to make sure you get the best results.
If you are taking the oral suspension, shake the bottle well for at least 20 seconds before each use.
Measure the medicine with an accurate measuring device, not a regular household spoon.
While using simvastatin, you may need frequent blood tests at your doctor's office.
You may need to take simvastatin on a long-term basis for the treatment of high cholesterol.
You may need to stop using simvastatin for a short time if you have surgery or a medical emergency.
Do not stop taking simvastatin unless your doctor tells you to.

chunks.text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to simvastatin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to simvastatin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Simvastatin can cause the breakdown of muscle tissue.
The breakdown of muscle tissue can lead to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain.
Call your doctor right away if you have tenderness.
Call your doctor right away if you have weakness.
Call your doctor right away if you have a fever.
Call your doctor right away if you have unusual tiredness.
Call your doctor right away if you have dark urine.
Also call your doctor at once if you have:
signs of a kidney problem - little or no urinating; painful or difficult urination; swelling in your feet or ankles; feeling tired or short of breath; or

chunks.section_heading: What other drugs will affect simvastatin?
chunks.text:
Many drugs can interact with simvastatin.
Not all possible interactions are listed here.
Tell your doctor about all your medications and any you start or stop using during treatment, especially:
delavirdine;
fenofibrate; or
fluconazole.
Your doctor may need to change your treatment plan.
This may happen if you use certain antibiotics or antifungal medicines.
It may also happen if you use heart medication.
It may also happen if you use antiviral medications.
Examples of antiviral medications include hepatitis C medications.
Examples of antiviral medications include HIV/AIDS medications.
Examples of antiviral medications include Paxlovid for COVID-19.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with simvastatin.
List includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.
